What it actually is

A voice agent that picks up your phone, holds a real conversation, and does something useful with it. It knows what you sell, what you charge for, when you are available, and what to do with a caller who needs a human.

The problem it solves is unglamorous and expensive: the call you missed. A missed call at a service business is usually a job that went to whoever answered on the second try.

Who this is for

Businesses where the phone is still the primary way work arrives, and where missing it costs real money:

  • Home services — plumbing, HVAC, electrical, roofing, pool. Emergency-heavy, seasonal, and the after-hours call is often the biggest job of the week.
  • Medical and dental practices where the front desk cannot answer three lines and a patient at the counter simultaneously.
  • Legal practices where intake quality determines whether a matter is worth taking.
  • Auto and specialty shops fielding the same pricing and availability questions all day.
  • Any business paying for an answering service that takes messages without answering anything.

What it does on a call

  • Answers immediately, at any hour, on every line at once. There is no hold queue and no second ring.
  • Answers the actual question — what you do, whether you cover that area, roughly what something costs, when you could come out.
  • Books into your calendar, respecting real availability rather than promising a slot you do not have.
  • Triages by call type. A burst pipe at 11pm and a question about store hours should not be handled the same way, and they are not.
  • Escalates to a human when the situation needs one, with the context already gathered.
  • Logs everything — transcript, outcome, captured details — so nothing depends on somebody remembering.

What it takes to set up

  1. Call inventory. We work out the call types you actually get. Most businesses have four or five, and they are not the ones on the website.
  2. Knowledge and rules. Services, service area, pricing boundaries, what it must never commit to, when it must hand off.
  3. Calendar and system connections. Whatever you already use for scheduling.
  4. Number routing. Usually it takes overflow and after-hours first. Taking every call from day one is possible, but starting at the edges is how you build trust in it.
  5. Listen and tighten. You review real calls in the first weeks. This always changes something.

What determines the cost

A build fee plus monthly capacity based on call volume and length. It is priced against what the alternative costs you — an answering service per message, a receptionist's salary, or the jobs currently going to voicemail.

Voice AI is one of the three products in the AI Business Starter Pack at a published price.

The objection we hear most

"My customers will hate talking to a robot."

Some will, and the honest answer is that the comparison is not against your best receptionist on a quiet morning. It is against voicemail, a hold queue, or a fourth ring at 9pm. Callers are markedly more tolerant of an AI that answers instantly and actually resolves the thing than of a human who never picks up.

The design decisions that matter: it says what it is, it hands off to a person without a fight, and it never traps someone in a loop. Where a caller wants a human, the goal is to get them one, not to win the call.

Questions people actually ask

Before you call

How long does an AI receptionist take to go live?

Days rather than months for a standard deployment. The work is mostly in the call inventory and the rules; the technology is the quick part. Complex calendar or dispatch integrations extend it.

Can it handle emergency calls?

Yes, and triage is usually the first rule we write. An emergency is identified from what the caller says and routed straight to whoever is on call, with the details captured. The worst possible outcome is an AI calmly booking a flooding bathroom for next week, so that path gets built and tested first.

Will it know our prices?

It knows whatever pricing rules you give it, and it is constrained to those. Most businesses give ranges and call-out fees rather than firm quotes, because a firm quote over the phone without seeing the job is a problem whether a human or an AI gives it.

What happens if it cannot help?

It says so, collects what it has, and gets the caller to a person or a callback. It does not improvise.

Can we keep our existing phone number?

Yes. Most deployments start by taking overflow and after-hours traffic on your existing number, so nothing about how customers reach you changes.
